page: Amazon Web Services m6g.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro system and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running on AWS Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 32 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache per core. No local instance storage or dedicated GPU accelerators are bundled, requiring users to rely on network-attached storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier multi-threaded execution balanced against lower single-thread efficiency. Multi-core evaluations show solid scaling, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8494.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 24287.64. Key operational metrics include static web serving throughput of 18.69 GB/sec, 18.83 million Redis SET operations per second, and a PassMark database score of 10352.18. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 965.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 20.29 GB/sec, and constrained token generation on large language model inference tasks.

The 1:1 ratio between vCPUs and physical cores ensures predictable, non-oversubscribed compute performance across concurrent threads, making this instance cost-efficient for scaled, multi-threaded workloads. However, the absence of local NVMe storage necessitates external volume provisioning, and lower single-thread clock speeds present a tradeoff for execution bottlenecks. The instance is suited for multi-threaded application servers, containerized microservices, Redis caching tiers, Clang-based compilation pipelines, and relational database hosting where single-thread latency is not paramount.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the 64-bit AWS Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM allocation. It lacks local storage and hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage over a 5 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark evaluations highlight average multi-threaded computational and memory capacity, achieving 18.83 million Redis SET operations per second and stable clang build metrics, alongside lower single-core execution performance and limited machine learning inference capabilities. The dedicated, non-hyperthreaded physical core architecture offers consistent throughput for multi-threaded services. Amazon Web Services m6g.4xlarge is practical for container fleets, caching infrastructure, web applications, and database engines that benefit from multi-core scalability.
